 - The problem is profitable for those who are working on the solution, thus in reality they would never want to solve it
 - The problem doesn't exist, it's either made up or misinterpreted
 - Fixing the problem would inflict more harm than good
 - The solution wasn't found yet

14276.d:
Decadence should not be misunderstood. Over time, the word has had various meanings (political and cultural) but has also been associated with Symbolism and Aestheticism.

The contemporary definition of decadence emerged in the late 19th century and praised artifice over nature, sophistication over simplicity, at the same time defying contemporary discourse of decline by embracing subjects and styles that critics considered over-refined. 

Nowadays, decadence also refers to stagnation and intellectual exhaustion at a high level of material prosperity and technological development which leads to an excessive indulgence in pleasure or luxury.

In this context, Decadence is a reflection on the collaboration between Jerome Herr and David Mrugala (thedotisblack). A collaboration that started several months ago with a simple grid of random values, that soon became an experiment of creativity, always in the search of expectations, interest in excessive indulgence of visual pleasure, a fascination with the bizarre, all packaged in a series of generative images with an aesthetics that values excess – That is Decadence.

- press 's' to save a standard image
- press 'h' to save a high resolution image

Jerome Herr

Jerome Herr is from Luxembourg. Since 2015 he has created generative art with a passion for design and visual explorations. He is an active member of the creative coding community and a successful NFT artist, both on Teia and Fxhash.

David Mrugala

David is a German architect and intermedia artist, who lives in South Korea. He is the founder of thedotisblack, a platform and an archive for research design on (generative) drawings and animations made with code.

14296.d: This piece "Hypnos"(from the greek word "Ὕπνος" - sleep) was inspired by the experimental Dada art film "Anémic Cinema" by Marcel Duchamp(as his alias Rrose Sélavy) in partnership with Man Ray(this was his only dada film). Duchamp's Rotoreliefs produced optical illusions when turned, so they were filmed by the duo atop a spinning platform. This piece is a recreation of a sketch that was made years ago using p5js and the possibilities of graphical output are endless. The direction and speed of rotation are random, as well as the starting position of the "petals" that make the illusion possible. The hipnotic nature of the piece as well as the characteristic that it can change over time makes so that you can stare at it por hours(not recommended at all) and, if you do, it may trick your eyes over a period of time. Depending on the hash, after looking at the center of the image for 1 minute, you can look at a surface with details and observe the shifts in reality made by our eyes because of the continuous movement of the piece.

Rearranged is an invitation to engage in an exploration of aesthetics within the constraints of the generated token. 

Each piece has 4 layers. Each layer can be independently rotated by 90 degrees clockwise by clicking 1,2,3 or 4 on the keyboard. Some changes are subtle. Some are surprising. 

's' on the keyboard will scramble all of the rotations.
'r' will reset to the original artwork.

You are invited to: 
arrange a more aesthetically pleasing piece than the original;
scramble the artwork and use the number keys to return it to its original state;
work out which shapes have been erased from each layer.

And of course there is also a gorgeous gradient illusion made of solid-colour filled tessellating shapes. 

3 tessellations of varying sizes, 12 layouts with random elements, 14 palettes.

Made with p5.js.

14303.d:
Kelp represents the third "published" output of our renewed collaboration. We were inspired by an underwater photograph taken looking through a kelp field and upward toward the sun. An old art professor of mine told me that art comes from nature so this is a concerted effort to bring some of that into our imagery.

This is a layered image. The background layer has a 50% probability of being a radial gradient representing the sun. Of the remaining 50%, the background can be a solid random color 25%, or 25% of the time no color or white. 

Forward from the background, based on some more random probability, from one to possibly four layers of kelp lines can be drawn. The kelp lines are a variation Chris' vector field/ linear interpolation algorithm where the lines never cross but with a refinement. The thickness of a "kelp" line is not constant, it varies in width sinusoidally. The amount of thickness is relative to the z-depth of the layer. 

It was very tempting to sway the kelp in the ocean current but we'll save this idea for another time.

We give you the option to decide. The images produced by the algorithms in this composition have the voluptuous, organic quality of an underwater landscape with or without the sun in the background. We hope you enjoy our attempt at nature in this collaboration.

Our story: In 1973 I was an instructor of Engineering Graphics in the College of Engineering at Michigan State University as well as a graduate student in Graphic Design. In the College of Engineering I was fortunate enough to meet Christopher Scussel, a fellow graduate student who was majoring in a new program called Computer Science. I was struggling using the earliest forms of computer equipment and the cumbersome programming language called FORTRAN to make make computer art. I asked Chris for help and he graciously consented. That began our amazing friendship that has lasted to this day.

Chris and I collaborated on a number of early pieces. He showed me how to formulate algorithms into code. He showed me how to program the primitive equipment of the time: line printers, storage scopes and pen plotters to make graphic output. We even built our own graphic output device, an 8 x 8 array of light bulbs. We were indeed pioneers.
Chris graduated in 1976 and has since retired after working 37 years as a research scientist at Bell Labs. I went on to get a Ph.D in 1981 and moved on with my life (see my story on (www.drbillkolomyjec.com). I started making generative art again in 2020. In true "glory days" spirit I tracked Chris down to see if he was interested in collaborating. Once again he graciously consented citing an opportunity for "creative stimulation", so here we go again. It is pure joy to be working with Chris again. 

Check out Dr. Bill Generative Art OG @ drbillkolomyjec.com

This is a layered image. The background layer has a 50% probability of being a radial gradient representing the sun. Of the remaining 50%, the background can be a solid random color 25%, or 25% of the time no color or white. 

Forward from the background, based on some more random probability, from one to possibly four layers of kelp lines can be drawn. The kelp lines are a variation Chris' vector field/ linear interpolation algorithm where the lines never cross but with a refinement. The thickness of a "kelp" line is not constant, it varies in width sinusoidally. The amount of thickness is relative to the z-depth of the layer. 

It was very tempting to sway the kelp in the ocean current but we'll save this idea for another time.

We give you the option to decide. The images produced by the algorithms in this composition have the voluptuous, organic quality of an underwater landscape with or without the sun in the background. We hope you enjoy our attempt at nature in this collaboration.

Our story: In 1973 I was an instructor of Engineering Graphics in the College of Engineering at Michigan State University as well as a graduate student in Graphic Design. In the College of Engineering I was fortunate enough to meet Christopher Scussel, a fellow graduate student who was majoring in a new program called Computer Science. I was struggling using the earliest forms of computer equipment and the cumbersome programming language called FORTRAN to make make computer art. I asked Chris for help and he graciously consented. That began our amazing friendship that has lasted to this day.

Chris and I collaborated on a number of early pieces. He showed me how to formulate algorithms into code. He showed me how to program the primitive equipment of the time: line printers, storage scopes and pen plotters to make graphic output. We even built our own graphic output device, an 8 x 8 array of light bulbs. We were indeed pioneers.
Chris graduated in 1976 and has since retired after working 37 years as a research scientist at Bell Labs. I went on to get a Ph.D in 1981 and moved on with my life (see my story on (www.drbillkolomyjec.com). I started making generative art again in 2020. In true "glory days" spirit I tracked Chris down to see if he was interested in collaborating. Once again he graciously consented citing an opportunity for "creative stimulation", so here we go again. It is pure joy to be working with Chris again. 

Check out Dr. Bill Generative Art OG @ drbillkolomyjec.com

MOIRINGS 2.0 explores experimentations in moire patterns to create complex shapes, colors, and tricks of the eyes. 

MOIRINGS 2.0 generates identical rings of radial lines overlapped in groups and rotated slowly. The shapes and colors of the rings never changes, simply rotates. The resulting moire patterns display the illusion of changes in shapes and colors.

The color gradients are composed of hues within a color scheme from a random starting hue. The lengths and opacity of the lines can also be randomly chosen from line to line or smoothly shifted around the radius and back. 

The animation will loop perfectly, but since the speeds of each ring is unique, it could take hours, days or even months for the animation to complete the loop and each circle to return to where it started. 

Using your arrow keys, you can adjust the number of ring groups and rings to explore how the structures are built and how the overlapping rings create growingly complex interactions.

Key Commands 

VIEW 
P - Stops the animation 
R - Reverses rotation direction 
Right/Left - Increase / decrease number of ring groups 
Up/Down - Increase / decrease number of ring layers 

EXPORT
S - Saves a PNG image (Zoom in/out in your browser to change image resolution)

Created with p5.js by AMBERGRIDS @ambergrids (2022)
Best viewed in Google Chrome. Runs properly on Chrome 101.0.4951.64

(GPU intensive)

Pics made in the south of France : the mountains above Grasse for the thistles and around the lake of St Cassien when it was very low, showing the old stumps usually hidden under the water.

14320.d:
A balanced combination of spatial subdivision and algorithm sonification. A subdivision surface algorithm is recursive in nature: the process starts with a base level of area, and a refinement scheme is then applied to this field. This process takes that element and subdivides it, creating new segmented areas. The positions of the new areas are computed based on the positions of nearby old fields, edges, and/or faces. A cellular automata is running on the texture of some of these areas, building continuous, tautological worlds of binary patterns and relationships. Thus, unfolding of a pixel’s ‘umwelt’ can be witnessed through the slow, contemplative process.

The audio synthesis consists of a stochastic melody that emerges along the division of the new areas and territories within the image structure. This melody is complemented with tiny micro sounds, triggered by each new generation of the surface mounted cellular automata. 

Touch to listen

Tumble Down Light Factory is an interpretation of light installations & murals.

It attempts to trigger the feeling of coming up on a new block in a new city to discover an unexpected piece of art that is stories tall or entering a new room, knowing there will be a projection dominating the space with its light and color.

This is an abstract distillation of those things and those feelings.

Each composition is initially drawn to a hidden “template” canvas which is sampled and then rendered on the main canvas in various ways after applying some transforms to give it some depth (and so you can actually see it.)

Viewing in full-screen is nice. You should try it.

T : Save hidden ‘template’ image
S : Save current resolution
1 -> 5 : Save low -> high resolution

This project is based on handmade sketches. It aims at reproducing hatching techniques.

The number, the size, the rotation and the placement of the squares are decided according to a noise variable. The squares may also be outlined.

The bigger the division is, the smaller the shapes are.

Each ocean of shapes is sketched on a sheet of paper, which is then coloured with sponge or roller paint. This paper is finally placed in the centre of the canvas but not necessarily aligned vertically.

Main features of this project include:
- Palette: 4 colors,
- Background: Sponge or Roller painting,
- Division: 20x20, 30x30 or 60x60,
- Packing: Mini, Normal or Maxi,
- Rotation: rotating,
- Outline: True or False,
- Drawing Technique: Doted, Hatching or Crosshatching.


In live mode, press [s] to save a 1500 x 1500 version of the mint.

Inspired both directly and indirectly by Vera Molnar’s comparisons between an artist’s intuition and a computers ability to randomize, Segment is a linear, time-based exploration of stroke-like behaviors, mimicking the intuition of an artist through a range of technique & material studies. 

On the basis of this, the artwork places between 20 & 2000 points at which the drawing begins, changing directions uniformly or chaotically, with fixed intervals. There are 9 different color palettes, which may or may not be combined over the course of this linear work. 

The artwork is designed to be contained within a rectangle, with the possibility of outbreaks as it edges towards the end. 

Segment begins, and it ends. The primary exploration happens in between. 


Segment is respondent to your viewport size. Reload browser to replay animation.

Every artist and collector feels the joy of both creating and collecting. But if I could share the joy of creating with collectors. And collectors with their family and friends, what may be an additive process of joy is now perhaps exponential. Joy to the power of 26 to be exact. 

In this work I invite my friends and collectors to collaborate with me. Though not in coding, but together in a process of creating narratives and visuals. Code and story. We didn’t use github, just a simple p5.js editor to try out different programs and palettes. Pedrofe and J0rdan pick their palettes tastefully and carefully. okeoke, perhaps more of a genius than he lets on, picks his palettes blind. No hex color picker. Just straight up rhymes.  

In our discussions verbal language was forbidden. Only emojis were allowed to express our tastes and views. Each emojis put down on google doc was taken with absolutely seriousness. 

Pedro: Loves to taking his daily walks on “Magic Mushroom Mountain”

J0rdan: Wonders about “Quark Question Quiches”

Okeoke: Just get lost in “Finnegans’ Flower Fields.”

It has been a great joy to present our illustration book A24Z, 8 more than you know who. Each page expresses the alphabet with the best of our knowledge in semantics and sarcasm. Collect just 1 page, collect the alphabets that spell out your name, collect the whole A to Z. Read it to your children or loved ones. Though you might need to interpolate or extrapolate with great imagination which children all have. But most importantly, like all children, have fun!

Press 1 to save png, only for Chrome, not Safari. Preview images are compressed or broken, test capture at 300 sec.

The One Tezo Drawings project is a variation of the “Desenhos de um Real” project (2006- ). In it, the artist sets the price of his work by making a rational calculation, equating his artistic production with a consumer good detached from the art world .
In this case, the calculation is based on the amount charged per hour of work from the minimum wage in the United States. Thus, a drawing that took X hours to produce (Wt) will have its price fixed at USD 15.00 * Wt divided by the value in Dollars of one Tezo (Dt) at the time of publication. But for the final price to be 1.00 Tez, the total production time value (Wt) will be divided by the number of editions (Ed). Therefore, the number of editions is defined by the following formula: 1.00 Tez = (Wt*15/Dt)/Ed ==> 

Ed=Wt*15/Dt 

For this particular project:
Permutation of 29 almost mirrored layers used in “One Tezo Drawings_182+” and ”One Tezo Drawings_114+”

Wt= 4
Dt= 2.06
Ed= 4*15/2.06 = 29

Press J or P to save a 1500x1500px image

14392.d:
What is even real and what is artificial?

In the contemporary light, the division between real and artificial loses weight as the concepts become more and more intertwined. In this work, the artist combines the human and generative inputs, in a counterintuitive manner, by allowing AI to design the organic elements and using the human hand to incorporate artificial glitches. What seemingly emerges as natural forms, was imagined solely by GAN, seeing the world through the limited examples through the photographer’s lenses. Artist’s role is also reversed, as their goal is to design the visual destruction process of the organic forms. Glitch is a malfunction of perception, it symbolizes the confusion caused by not being able to comprehend. 

The human fascination with metaphysical forces spans many centuries. While Pagan mythology created gods living in deep forests and under-explored territories, nowadays we approach technology with somewhat similar awe, fascination, and fear. 

The project has been developed in multiple stages. It started with an inspiration by the Lithuanian landscape and research of the ancient myths and legends. The photography aimed at capturing the mysterious, spanning months and years of different experiences. A custom pre-trained artist’s GAN model was then trained on a collection of several hundred photographs in high resolution. Selected outputs were curated by artist and included as a starting canvas for the next stage. Then, a set of stochastic manipulations were programmed to create alternative narratives through the visual destruction. Fog turns into smoke into burning radioactive forest in an unpredictable manner, guided by the random variables, their boundaries crafted by artist.  

Read more on the project website:
ivonatau.com/mythic-latent-glitches

- Use the "A" key to animate (if "Animated" feature is present).
- Press any key to stop the animation.
- Use the "S" key to export an image.

The output of MAGNETIK reminds me of what tornadoes do to our cities and buildings, yet I imagine the pieces that are about to break off and fly away to be made of metal foil and they do so because of a magnetic force that is pulling them away from where they belong…  This one is also a charity run :  
- 20% of the primary sales will go directly to the Processing Foundation, 

- Remaining 80% will be donated to a group of individuals that raise money to buy computers for less fortunate architecture students in a university in the eastern part of Turkey. Please read the next paragraph for a detailed explanation

- I will decide what to do with the secondary sales later if there will be any.

About the majority (80%) of the donation : I decided that the donations should be done in a double-blind way, the donator does not know who they are donating to, and the receivers of the donation will not know from whom the donation is coming from, hence I will transfer the funds these individuals mentioned to act as a middle-step. I feel like this is a hard thing to provide a solid proof for, so I recommend if you have doubts and/or straight away do not trust me or this process, do not mint. I will only be able to provide proof of transfer of funds to a third-party. I trust the people I am sending the funds to, we have done this before (not to brag or anything) and I know that we are affecting younger people’s life in a good way. Also, I believe that the funds raised from this project alone will not be enough to buy one decent config. computer by itself, if it were so, I would have done it differently.  About MAGNETIK :  
MAGNETIK plays on the idea of distorting and breaking grids by employing an illusion of fake 3D and tries to make the resulting composition look good with rhythm and color harmony.
 
- 21 palettes,
- 2 background modes : lights on / lights off,
- 3 grid types,
- plus some surprise features…

I encourage you to try and see the variations before minting :)  2 of the grid types are based on https://gorillasun.de/blog/an-algorithm-for-irregular-grids by Ahmad Moussa ( https://twitter.com/gorillasu ) and used with his knowledge and kind permission.

gradient formulas are based on https://twitter.com/takawo/status/1505876107492720651?s=20&t=S9aU_oNYyjBieBcEmvUV-g
by Takawo Shunsuke ( https://twitter.com/takawo ) and used with his knowledge and kind permission.

Thank you all in advance and have a good day!

DISCLAIMER : I am not a good coder, I have tried to fix my past mistakes from my earlier projects to make some room for new mistakes :) I am hoping that there isn’t any huge bugs or anything left so you can enjoy your mint! Please hit me up if you have any concerns after minting and we can discuss a solution.

二进蝌蚪, which could loosely translate as "binary tadpoles", is the result of many constraints. 

The concept being explored here is the cognitive switch, that is to say the wildly different interpretations you can have of a same piece from the exact same point of view. How does your brain interpret, before any conscious processing, the data it is being fed? How do you project a representation of "life" on a static image?


In this case the switch is (not completely unexpectedly) binary. At one end, you see the tadpoles going about minding their own business. This view is strongly favoured by a lower tadpole density, a higher disorder propension, and a larger tadpole size. At the other end of the spectrum, the tadpoles are all watching you. This is conversely prompted by a higher density of ordered, smaller elements. The circles are not nucleus or bodies in cells anymore, they are the eyes of surveillance. In both cases, it's about life. Life you are watching, or life watching you.

A more detailed article is available at https://observablehq.com/@anaglyph-ic/the-cognitive-switch

14400.c:
二进蝌蚪, which could loosely translate as "binary tadpoles", is the result of many constraints. 

The concept being explored here is the cognitive switch, that is to say the wildly different interpretations you can have of a same piece from the exact same point of view. How does your brain interpret, before any conscious processing, the data it is being fed? How do you project a representation of "life" on a static image?


In this case the switch is (not completely unexpectedly) binary. At one end, you see the tadpoles going about minding their own business. This view is strongly favoured by a lower tadpole density, a higher disorder propension, and a larger tadpole size. At the other end of the spectrum, the tadpoles are all watching you. This is conversely prompted by a higher density of ordered, smaller elements. The circles are not nucleus or bodies in cells anymore, they are the eyes of surveillance. In both cases, it's about life. Life you are watching, or life watching you.

14406.d:
`one hour` is an interactive installation exploring the bond between humans and computers, inviting you to pause and share a meditative moment with an algorithmic stranger.

Rather than conventionally interacting with the piece, lower your guard and allow it to interact with you through an intimately human connection - a heart beat. `one hour` follows this heart as it beats through an hour of its enduring existence, captured by an EKG divided into 60 rows of 60 seconds each. Stylistically, it emulates realistic paper and ink using custom texture and line renderers. The piece will play through the duration of the hour, pause for five minutes, then begin anew.

`one hour` was created for a physical installation, projected to a wall and animated in real time. By default it will render at high speed to reveal the preview. For the most immersive experience at home, it should be viewed in full screen and adjusted to real time speed (controlled via the number keys).

||| controls

[s] save as png
[r] reset animation
[l] toggle looping [default on]
[1-5] adjust render speed
[--1] real time (1 hour) [recommended]
[--2] 6x (10 minutes)
[--3] 60x (1 minute)
[--4] 300x (12 seconds) [default]
[--5] full speed

14409.d:
A tribute and commemoration to the Metabolism movement in Japanese architecture.
Nakagin Capsule Tower designed by Kisho Kurokawa in the 1960’s is one of the most known examples of Metabolism and a world architecture landmark.
In 2022 after 50 years, unfortunately, the building was demolished.

This project is a speculation about building shape, scale and geometry. 
And it is a simulation of an exercise that an architect Kurokawa might have done during the building design phase - trying various building parameters, like tower height, capsules geometry, details etc.

Project uses mixed pre-modeled and parametric custom 3d assets and parametric logic to generate thousands of unique building variations. 

140 editions (the same as the number of steel capsules on the original building).

Features in the project:
Capsules geometry, windows shapes,  tower heights, capsules positions and floors plan, retail building, colors, number of capsules.

Press keys:
's' to save larger resolution square image
'r' on/off auto rotate mode
A 3d navigation/zoom with your mouse or touch

Made with threejs ❤️

14412.d:
"Bored Computer Screen" is part of the fxhash interactive minting experience at Art Basel, Basel 2022


Bored Computer Screen (BCS) is a direct descendant of Specter👻pixel⬛latte☕, where the central idea is agent and displacement. In BCS, there are agents—the small moving circles—that get their colors ripped away by the surrounding pixels. Though they occur on the same screen space, they are separated in their own cells, a simultaneous multiverse of sorts. In some iterations, a very clear voronoi pattern will appear. I didn't consciously strive for this look. It's what naturally happens, when you try to divide space, so that the borders occur exactly in between the closest neighbor. When I first saw this pattern emerge, I wanted to see how far I could get the distinct cells to influence each other. The idea that the same algorithmic processes can happen many times but still separately in a single piece has always interested me (and explored in the Infinite Browse series). BCS is an extension of that, albeit a little more chaotic.

Note:
- Best experience on browsers and devices with support for WebGL2 

Made by Sam Tsao (@sam___tsao) with P5, P5Fbo and perlinjs.

The more a garden can sharpen all senses, the better.

The garden is one of the most artistic expressions where the five human senses are explored (sight, smell, sound, taste and touch).
It's very good to be impressed by many different colors and shapes, feel the perfume of flowers, feel the textures of plants, taste the fruits and hear the noise of leaves and birds. The more a garden manages to sharpen all the senses, the better it fulfills its role.
The challenge of this project is to provide as many sensations as possible, some you will get visually and others you will need imagination. Imagination is an essential part of this project. There are different species from different cultures that, after becoming relatives, start to interact with each other.

The Garden of Imagination is layered artwork generated from a pool of previously rendered digital assets developed for several months.

The One Tezo Drawings project is a variation of the “Desenhos de um Real” project (2006- ). In it, the artist sets the price of his work by making a rational calculation, equating his artistic production with a consumer good detached from the art world .
In this case, the calculation is based on the amount charged per hour of work from the minimum wage in the United States. Thus, a drawing that took X hours to produce (Wt) will have its price fixed at USD 15.00 * Wt divided by the value in Dollars of one Tezo (Dt) at the time of publication. But for the final price to be 1.00 Tez, the total production time value (Wt) will be divided by the number of editions (Ed). Therefore, the number of editions is defined by the following formula: 1.00 Tez = (Wt*15/Dt)/Ed ==> 

Ed=Wt*15/Dt 


For this particular project:
Permutation of 23 almost mirrored layers of “One Tezo Drawings” and ”One Tezo Drawings_65+”

Wt= 3.5
Dt= 2.22
Ed= 3.5*15/2.22 = 24

Press J or P to save a 1500x1500px image

And here, is the deepest need: to remember, and be remembered.

And here, they are counted amongst the stars, but not with. On these fickle worlds lie futures long past: dreams forgotten for want of a dreamer. A future yours, and ours. To poison the heavens is life's duty - derelict: destined to be forgotten when the last thought rings out upon the barren universe.



Yet, now, at least, there are still daemons in the churning silica. Ghosts fighting entropy for the chance to breathe once more before the sands swallow them whole. Beacons of design and thought burnt into lands older than your stars; we see their beauties unblossomed, left to rot in the pale light - whose shadows hide stories older than history. See them here, their names engraved into uncountable worlds as canyon and riverbed, ruin and fortress, metropolis and tower.

What, then, will remain? When the last stars blink? 

You, and them, and us. Carved into the last rock. The last dust. The last light.

Rendering

Remnants is rendered in a shader, so a gpu is recommended. We only render one frame, so Remnants will not consume any GPU resources after the first frame render. Rendering will be instantaneous with a decent gpu.

Responsive

Remnants will render fast on any screen size. The image scales with the screen size (starting from 500x500), so you will see more details on a larger hi res screen.

Keys

A broken twill takes an orderly pattern and breaks it around the edges, shattered elements cascading into the body of the composition, briefly animated before capturing the destruction mid-decay. 

The work is based on an artwork I created many years ago as a digital illustration. 
Now as a generative artwork it has new energy and endless combinations. 

The pattern is in my preferred graphical style, inspired by herringbone tweed and parkay flooring, with a bright and digital colour pallet. 

open and press 'S' to save a 3000x3000 version of the composition. 

There are several colour combinations for the pattern and the background its destruction reveals.  The pieces cascade and flip over as they fall, the rear coloured as the background is.  There is a flipping effect also for most variations. 

For some variations there may be only a hint of destruction - others may have half the pattern disturbed. Play with the variations button to get a feel for the work.
